who-top-causes.name: WHO: the top 10 causes of death (Global Health Estimates, 2023)

ischaemic-heart-disease.name: Ischaemic heart disease
ischaemic-heart-disease.passage: The world's biggest killer is ischaemic heart disease, responsible for 16% of the world's total deaths.

stroke.name: Stroke
stroke.passage: Stroke and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease were the second and third leading causes of deaths in 2023.

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.passage: Stroke and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease were the second and third leading causes of deaths in 2023.

lower-respiratory-infections.name: Lower respiratory infections
lower-respiratory-infections.passage: In 2023 it claimed 2.7 million lives, returning back up to its 2019 pre-pandemic level.

alzheimers-dementia.name: Alzheimer's disease and other dementias
alzheimers-dementia.passage: Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia ranked as the fifth leading cause of death, killing 2.1 million people.

diabetes.name: Diabetes
diabetes.passage: claiming 2.0 million lives, more than double the deaths in 2000

lung-cancer.name: Trachea, bronchus and lung cancers
lung-cancer.passage: Trachea, bronchus and lung cancers deaths have risen from 1.1 million in 2000 to 1.8 million in 2023.

kidney-diseases.name: Kidney diseases
kidney-diseases.passage: Kidney diseases have risen from the world's seventeenth leading cause of death to the ninth.

covid-19.name: COVID-19 (fourteenth in 2023)
covid-19.passage: Falling to 0.9 million globally, making it the fourteenth leading cause of death.

sdg-goal3.name: UN SDG Goal 3 targets (good health and well-being)

3.1.name: 3.1 Maternal mortality
3.1.passage: By 2030, reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births

3.2.name: 3.2 Deaths of newborns and children under 5
3.2.passage: By 2030, end preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5 years of age

3.3.name: 3.3 Epidemics and communicable diseases
3.3.passage: By 2030, end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases

3.4.name: 3.4 Non-communicable diseases, mental health and well-being
3.4.passage: By 2030, reduce by one third premature mortality from non-communicable diseases

3.5.name: 3.5 Substance abuse
3.5.passage: Strengthen the prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drug abuse and harmful use of alcohol

3.6.name: 3.6 Road traffic deaths and injuries
3.6.passage: By 2020, halve the number of global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents

3.7.name: 3.7 Sexual and reproductive health-care services
3.7.passage: By 2030, ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health-care services

3.8.name: 3.8 Universal health coverage
3.8.passage: Achieve universal health coverage, including financial risk protection

3.9.name: 3.9 Deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals and pollution
3.9.passage: By 2030, substantially reduce the number of deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals

3.a.name: 3.a Tobacco control
3.a.passage: Strengthen the implementation of the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control

3.b.name: 3.b Research on and access to affordable medicines and vaccines
3.b.passage: Support the research and development of vaccines and medicines for the communicable and non-communicable diseases

3.c.name: 3.c Health financing and health workforce
3.c.passage: Substantially increase health financing and the recruitment, development, training

3.d.name: 3.d Early warning and management of health risks
3.d.passage: Strengthen the capacity of all countries, in particular developing countries
